hook: A cluttered living room full of things to find: tap each object in the picture, then give it its article.
intro: A picture hunt instead of a deck: one lived-in, slightly cluttered living room with 32 things to find in it, every one a noun you meet when people talk about running a home and saving energy — der Heizkörper, das Bügeleisen, die Steckdosenleiste, das Windrad outside the window. The prompt asks Wo ist der Wäschekorb? and you tap it in the picture. Each find shows its label, coloured by its gender, then leaves a small tick in that colour, so you can see what you have already found. Once you have passed a run, the hunt turns harder: the prompt hides the article (Wo ist ___ Wäschekorb?), and after the find you choose der, die or das yourself. A tap on bare wall costs nothing; a tap on the wrong object tells you what you hit and you keep looking, and after three misses the right one is shown. No object is asked twice in the same run.
tips[0].title: Compounds in the eco flat: the last part decides
tips[0].text: Most of these words are compounds, and the last part decides the article. Steckdose + Leiste: die Leiste, so die Steckdosenleiste. Licht + Schalter: der Schalter, so der Lichtschalter. Find the last word and you have the article.
tips[0].check.why: The last part is der Ständer, so the whole word is der Wäscheständer.
tips[1].title: Devices in -er are masculine — but not -meter
tips[1].text: A thing that does a job, named with -er, is masculine: der Rauchmelder, der Lichtschalter, der Heizkörper. Words ending in -meter that measure something are the exception you see on every wall: das Thermometer.
tips[1].check.why: Measuring instruments in -meter are neuter: das Thermometer, das Barometer.
tips[2].title: Say the article out loud with every find
tips[2].text: When the label appears, read it aloud with its article: der Heizkörper, die Gießkanne. The colour on the label is the same one the deck and the Word Library use — blue der, red die, green das — so the picture trains your eye as well as your ear.
tips[2].check.why: The last part is das Rad, so the compound is das Windrad.
remember[0]: The last part of a compound sets the article: die Steckdose + die Leiste → die Steckdosenleiste.
remember[1]: -er devices are der (der Rauchmelder); -meter instruments are das (das Thermometer).
remember[2]: Das Altpapier has no plural: it is the paper you put out for recycling.
